subject: seasonal probability of detecton (and CIs) from occu model

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: seasonal probability of detecton (and CIs) from occu model
parts:
Greetings all,

I'd like to calculate seasonal probabilities of detection (and confidence intervals) across sites using a simple occu() model.

Here are detection probabilites from a single site surveyed twice. predict(fm,type='det')[1:2,] produces

  Predicted         SE     lower     upper
1 0.9014169 0.03904525 0.7944400 0.9558175
2 0.5551697 0.13061180 0.3068224 0.7787125

Using the estimates above, the seasonal probability of detecting the species at least once at this site would be

1 - (1 - 0.901)*(1 - 0.555) = 0.956

Does anyone know how might I calculate confidence intervals around this estimate?

Many thanks.
Giancarlo

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] seasonal probability of detecton (and CIs) from occu model
parts:
Dear Giancarlo,

you could use the delta rule, which can be implemented using functions in R packages msm and car for instance.

Alternatively, you could fit the model bayesianly with an MCMC engine, specify this function as a derived quantity and then get the uncertainty for free, as usual.

Best regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] seasonal probability of detecton (and CIs) from occu model
parts:
Here is a brute force approach using the Delta method.  (I can supply the details for the estimate of the standard error later this week when I have more time.)

# Two-visit example to get approximate confidence intervals for big P

# Load library
  library(unmarked)
  
# Generate some data from known parameters
# Number of sites
  n <- 100
# Site status
  psi <- 0.8 # Probability of occupancy
  status <- rbinom(n,1,psi)
# Observation status
  p1 <- 0.90
  y1 <- rbinom(n,1,p1)
  p2 <- 0.56
  y2 <- rbinom(n,1,p2)
  y <- status*matrix(c(y1,y2),byrow=FALSE,nrow=n)
# Visit number
  visit =matrix(rep(c("1","2"),n),byrow=TRUE,nrow=n)
  
# Make unmarked data frame
  udf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y,obsCovs=list(visit=visit))
  
# Run occu
  results = occu(~ visit ~ 1, udf)

# Get estimates
  # logits of detection parameters from occu
  intercept = results@estimates@estimates$det@estimates[1]
  visit2 = results@estimates@estimates$det@estimates[2]
  # Covariance matrix of detection logits
  covmat = results@estimates@estimates$det@covMat
  # Detection probabilities for visits 1 and 2
  p1.mle = 1 - 1/(1+exp(intercept))
  p2.mle = 1 - 1/(1+exp(intercept+visit2))
  # Probability of at least one detection at an occupied site
  bigP.mle = 1 - (1-p1.mle)*(1-p2.mle)
  # Approximate standard error of bigP using the Delta method
    bigP.se = ((exp(2*intercept)*(covmat[1,1]*(1 + exp(visit2) +
      2*exp(intercept + visit2))^2 + exp(visit2)*(1 + exp(intercept))*
      (covmat[2,2]*exp(visit2)*(1 + exp(intercept)) + 2*covmat[1,2]*(1 + exp(visit2) + 
      2*exp(intercept + visit2)))))/ ((1 + exp(intercept))^4*
      (1 + exp(intercept + visit2))^4))^0.5
  # Approximate confidence intervals for bigP
  lower95 = max(0,bigP.mle - 1.96*bigP.se)
  upper95 = min(1,bigP.mle + 1.96*bigP.se)
 
# Summarize results
  cat("True bigP = 1 - (1-p1)*(1-p2) = ",1 - (1-p1)*(1-p2)," ")
  cat("Estimate of bigP = ",bigP.mle," ")
  cat("Approximate 95% confidence interval for bigP = (",lower95,",",upper95,") ")

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] seasonal probability of detecton (and CIs) from occu model
parts:
Well, it was much simpler than I made it out to be.  If one has no observation covariates other than the visit number (as a string), then running occu with

     results = occu(~ -1 + visit ~ 1, udf)

such that each visit gets an explicit logit to itself, life becomes much simpler.  Below is the updated example still with just 2 visits in the simulated data but the formulas for the standard error (and confidence intervals) will work with any number of visits.  (Someone must have done this before but I'm sorry not to know who that is.)

# Two-visit example to get approximate confidence intervals for big P

# Load library
  library(unmarked)
  
# Generate some data from known parameters
# Number of sites
  n <- 100
# Site status
  psi <- 0.8 # Probability of occupancy
  status <- rbinom(n,1,psi)
# Observation status
  p1 <- 0.90
  y1 <- rbinom(n,1,p1)
  p2 <- 0.56
  y2 <- rbinom(n,1,p2)
  y <- status*matrix(c(y1,y2),byrow=FALSE,nrow=n)
# Visit number
  visit =matrix(rep(c("1","2"),n),byrow=TRUE,nrow=n)
  
# Make unmarked data frame
  udf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y,obsCovs=list(visit=visit))
  
# Run occu

results = occu(~ -1 + visit ~ 1, udf)

# Covariance matrix for logits
  covmat = results@estimates@estimates$det@covMat

# Detection probabilities for each visit
  p.mle <- matrix(1 - 1/(1+exp(results@estimates@estimates$det@estimates)),nrow=1)

# Approximate standard error for big P
  bigP.se <- prod(1-p.mle)*(p.mle %*% covmat %*% t(p.mle))^0.5

# Approximate confidence intervals for bigP
  lower95 = max(0,bigP.mle - 1.96*bigP.se)
  upper95 = min(1,bigP.mle + 1.96*bigP.se)
 
# Summarize results
  cat("True bigP = 1 - (1-p1)*(1-p2) = ",1 - (1-p1)*(1-p2)," ")
  cat("Estimate of bigP = ",bigP.mle," ")
  cat("Approximate 95% confidence interval for bigP = (",lower95,",",upper95,") ")

messages.author: 0227543d81e2924c
messages.subject: Re: seasonal probability of detecton (and CIs) from occu model
parts:
People have helpfully pointed to R packages, or provided code snippets. All good, but if you want to understand what you're doing (as opposed to 'plugging and chugging', there are any number of good references out there on the Delta method (Appendix in the occupancy book, Appendix in Williams, Nichols & Conroy,...). A more comprehensive, albeit wordy treatment of the subject (the author is prone to such things) can be found here:

http://www.phidot.org/software/mark/docs/book/pdf/app_2.pdf

A simpler entre is nicely presented in Larkin Powell's paper, here: 

http://snr.unl.edu/powell/research/powell_07.pdf

And, as Marc points out, the Delta approximation isn't needed if you 'go Bayesian', but that requires a greater level of investment than you might want for your present purposes.
